headline: An AI security system found a decade-old flaw in the XRP Ledger that could have let an attacker create trillions of new XRP coins, and an emergency patch closed it.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered by 1: the flaw was patched on 25 Sep and disclosed on 9 Oct 2026, before the window, and the scale figures are Veria's own.
importance_line: Holders and users of XRP faced a risk of coins being created from nothing that is now closed, but the 18 trillion figure comes from Veria Labs, and the case shows AI tools finding flaws that audits missed in old code.
summary: CryptoSlate reports that the security firm Veria Labs says its AI-powered system found two linked weaknesses in the software behind the XRP Ledger (the network that records XRP cryptocurrency payments) that could have let an attacker create about 18 trillion XRP, roughly 180 times the original supply, with a single payment. RippleX, which works on that software, patched it within three days of the 22 Sep 2026 report, skipping its usual validator vote, and later confirmed that no XRP was created improperly and no funds were lost; the flaw was publicly disclosed on 9 Oct 2026.
notes: Read in full on CryptoSlate; Veria and RippleX documents not opened. Underlying events date from 22 to 25 Sep and 9 Oct 2026, so the score is lowered for age.
